score.purpose: The reach numeral beside the board; steps down to 48, 32 and 24px.

display.purpose: Sheet titles and the STEWARD lettering.

title.purpose: Buttons, the day plate, event, slip and option-group titles.

body-lead.purpose: The question being asked, in the dialog.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked labels: measures, tools, fields, key caps.

shadows.name: ring-quiet
shadows.purpose: Plates and pieces lying flat; the ring colour changes on hover, selection or outcome.

shadows.name: ring
shadows.purpose: Pieces standing on the table: board, drawer, buttons, event cards.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Question cards; the ring takes the suit colour.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and sheets, the highest pieces.

shadows.name: well
shadows.purpose: Inputs, selects, unlit tokens and puzzle tiles on an ink face; cyan on focus.

shadows.name: lettering-split
shadows.purpose: text-shadow on the STEWARD lettering only.

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: Timing for every transition and arrival; pixel things move in steps.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Cards and slips dealt in, dialogs lifting, the drawer sliding (16px to 24px travel with a stepped fade).

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Failing measures and processing state; 0.5s for a late timer, 1.2s for the alarm ring.

motion.name: reduced
motion.purpose: Collapses all animation and transition durations.

narrative.overview:
The screen is a table at night with a pixel board game laid on it. The colony is the board, ring-framed in the centre; its score track runs round the frame in gold pips; the world's measures stand as segmented tracks beside it; the settlers' questions are playing cards fanned along the bottom edge, the most urgent one raised and largest. A pixel sky band sits across the top and carries the lettering, the day and the clock. Nothing here is a panel of a dashboard: every surface is a physical game piece (a board, a card, a slip, a token, a sheet) placed on the table.

Every piece is built the same way: a square face, a 2px gap of ink, a hard coloured ring, and on the pieces that sit proud of the table a hard plinth beneath. There are no rounded corners, no blurred shadows and no eased motion; things are drawn on a grid and move in steps. Two pixel faces carry all text, Silkscreen for lettering and VT323 for reading, with font smoothing switched off. The canvas board and sky are rendered pixelated and draw their pieces as flat blocks outlined in ink.

Colour is semantic and sparing against the navy table. Cyan is the player's own signal, gold is reach and insight, coral is reserved for what is critical or lost, and each question topic owns one suit colour that follows it from the card's ring to its corner icon to its measure track.
keyCharacteristics: One frame recipe for every piece: face, 2px ink gap, hard ring, hard plinth.
Square everywhere; the radius scale has one step and it is zero.
Pixel type with smoothing off; Silkscreen only at multiples of 8px.
Stepped motion (`steps(4, end)`), stepped blinks, no easing curves.
Quantities are counted pieces: ten-segment tracks, pips, tokens, never smooth bars.
Authored 8 by 8 pixel icons that inherit the colour of what they mark.

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: Cyan is you, gold is reach and insight, coral is critical or lost. None of the three is ever used as decoration or to mean anything else.

rules.name: The Suit Rule
rules.body: A topic has exactly one colour, passed down as `--suit` (pieces) or `--c` (tracks), and it colours the ring, the corner icons and the timer together. A critical question overrides its suit with coral; a council question with gold.

rules.name: The Quiet Ring Rule
rules.body: A piece that is not asking for anything wears a `line` ring. Colour on a ring is a claim on the player's attention.

rules.name: The Eight Grid Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen is set only at multiples of 8px (16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64); that is its pixel grid, and off it the letters smear.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight is always 400. Emphasis inside running text is a change of colour (ice inside dim, gold for a count), never bold.

rules.name: The Counted Numbers Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes while you watch uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: Every frame is face, 2px ink gap, hard ring. Frames are drawn with `box-shadow` spread, never with `border`.

rules.name: The Plinth Rule
rules.body: Only pieces that stand on the table cast a plinth, and the plinth is always straight down, solid, and in `plinth`. A pressed button sinks 2px and its plinth shortens by the same.

rules.name: The Height Rule
rules.body: Ring width is height: 4px lies flat, 5px stands, 6px is lifted above everything.

dos: Do build every new piece from the frame recipe: face, 2px ink gap, hard ring via `box-shadow` spread, and a straight-down `plinth` drop only if it stands on the table.
Do pick ring width by height: 4px flat, 5px standing, 6px lifted.
Do set Silkscreen at 16, 24, 32, 40, 48 or 64px, uppercase, tracked 1px to 2px; set everything read in VT323.
Do carry a topic's colour through `--suit` so ring, icons and timer change together.
Do show quantities as counted square cells: ten segments, pips or tokens.
Do draw new icons on the 8 by 8 grid in `public/src/icons.js`, one weight, inheriting `currentColor`.
Do move things with `steps()` timing over 0.2s to 0.3s and blink with two-step loops; keep the reduced-motion collapse.
Do keep text on the table at `ice`, `dim` or `mute`, and text on cyan or gold faces at `ink`.
donts: Don't round a corner. There is no radius in this system.
Don't blur a shadow or use a glow; depth is ring width and a hard plinth.
Don't draw a frame with `border`; rings must not take layout space.
Don't ease or spring motion; nothing in the build uses a curve.
Don't use coral for anything that is not critical, failing or lost, or gold for anything that is not reach, insight, council or the Ark.
Don't use bold; the faces ship in one weight and emphasis is colour.
Don't set Silkscreen off its 8px grid, or use it for running text.
Don't use a smooth progress bar where a counted track would do.
Don't bring in an icon font, emoji or outline icon set; icons are the authored pixel set.
Don't add a light theme; the world is declared dark-only.
